lines.x: Everything on the to-do list is done! Is there anything else for me? Your schedule, the financial statements... What? You can't put me in charge of those? Why not? I'm very good at that sort of thing!
I saw that, Doctor. What did you just hide behind your back—is that a soda? Cut back a little, it's bad for your teeth. I'll be taking this can, thank you.

I just ran into a big name from Saluzzo Vino out in the corridor. If I get the chance, I'd love to have a meal with him—and if I get a better chance, talk a little business. Afraid of him? Of course not. He and I are the same: we both do it for our family. I think he'd understand me.

Things go bad if you let them sit, so I'm not fond of 'let's talk about it later.' If it can be dealt with now, deal with it now. Doctor, the fruit I cut for you half an hour ago—why haven't you touched it? Still in a remote meeting? Tell them to wait. Eat the fruit, right now.

Don't worry about me. Some problems you don't handle after you've figured them out—you just have to get through today, and tomorrow there'll be a way. As long as tomorrow still comes, nothing is over yet. Right after what happened to Mama Paula, I told myself that over and over, every single day.

I think I understand a little now, why Mama Paula founded the orchestra. Birth and blood—those can hold a family together, of course. But so can people who huddle close for warmth, people who share the same dream. They can become family too. I really do wish she could see it.

The orchestra members do think I fuss too much sometimes. But I can't help it—once I care about someone, I can't just glance their way and leave them be. I'm still learning where to draw the line, little by little, from Hibiscus. So if I ever start to bother you, Doctor, you have to tell me.

I used to just help Mama Paula with things around the house. Errands, scheduling, keeping the books. Before I knew it, that had grown to cover the whole orchestra, and there were more and more habits I had to remember. Still—even if I had to memorize a hundred more of your habits, Doctor, no problem at all.

Doctor, where is your hometown? Have you always simply been 'the Doctor of Rhodes Island'? Sometimes I'm not sure myself—am I Siracusan, or a Leithanian living in Siracusa? And where is the place I belong? For now, at least, let me be Rhodes Island's Ripresa for a while.
Doctor? Doctor~ Doc—tor— Huh, it's not like the concert hall. The sound bounces back.

So you're our orchestra's new partner? You have a good eye—we're not just 'an orchestra of Leithanians,' you know. Oh, I almost forgot to introduce myself. I'm the orchestra's manager. Codename: Ripresa.
Bringing out everyone's strengths in exactly the right place... that really is no easy thing.
Doctor, may I apply to found an orchestra here on Rhodes Island now?
So as not to let that expectation down—Doctor, could you also fund me for some further study at a university? I'd like to go deeper into management.
Which side of it do you need me for? Just say the word~
Leading a whole crowd into negotiations again? Lucky for us, I've got plenty of experience by now.
Hold on, let me look over the arrangements one more time before we go... All right, we can move.
They don't look like they came to negotiate, do they?
Good eye.
No problem!
Nothing difficult about it.
I can adapt.
Let's finish it in one go!
I'm a professional, you know!
Once it's begun, there's no reason to stop halfway.
This flame—it is my unyielding heart.
D-Doctor, you really are incredible! Teach me. Next time, I want to lead everyone the way you do.
I did great! Every arrangement paid off. Well done, me.
Holding out to the end is already plenty good! It's fine—I'll do better next time, so keep up with me, Doctor!
I won't admit defeat. I'll carry everyone through this. Here, let me see your injuries first—is everyone all right?
No problem! Let me first see how things run around here.
Whoa—honestly, Doctor, could you please get back to work? I'm busy too, you know.
I did pretty well, didn't I! Praise me a little more~
Arknights.

Happy New Year, Doctor! Back when I lived with Mama Paula, she always said you should do some small thing that stands for good luck on the first day of the year. I thought it over, and decided to start with a wish. We can gather up our luck slowly over the year to come—no need to rush~
I've already sorted out today's business. Where would you like to start, Doctor?

Happy birthday, Doctor! You worry about enough as it is. Today you're not allowed to think about anything—leave it all to me. First, come hear my recital, then a truly lavish Siracusan dinner... Doctor, wait, you really don't need to go dig out formal wear—

Huh, has it really been this long since we met, Doctor? So much happened this year—looking back on it still leaves me a little dazed. But that's fine. I got used to looking forward a long time ago, and I know who's standing beside me. Put that way, the future isn't so hard at all.
